newsitem.title: ITALY: Lira in ERM end-Nov at 1,000/1,050/mark - minister.
newsitem.headline: Lira in ERM end-Nov at 1,000/1,050/mark - minister.

text.p: Italian Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said Italy expected to return the lira to Europe's exchange rate mechanism by the end of November, with 1,000-1,050 per mark seen as the best rate.
Visco told a meeting of the former communist Democratic Party of the Left in Rome late on Thursday: "Within this month we must enter the (exchange rate mechanism)."

"I think a balanced solution with the mark between 1,000 and 1,050 lire would be more than reasonable, especially as we are in a situation in which we still have a little potential competitive advantage," he said.
The lira is currently trading at 1,005.05/5.35 per mark and has held steady around 1,000-1,010 recently.
Visco also said he thought the Bank of Italy had ample room to cut the official discount rate, "and, if the budget goes through, there will be another reduction."
The discount rate is currently at 7.50 percent after the central bank lopped 75 basis points from it on October 24.
The lower house of parliament is currently voting on the individual articles of the 1997 draft budget.
